span.label: A CURATED, VERSIONED, EVIDENCE-BEARING KNOWLEDGEBASE OF WHAT GENES DO - and the rules by which its terms are added, merged, obsoleted and traced back to the paper that justified them
span.quote: The GO knowledgebase consists of three components: (1) the GO—a computational knowledge structure describing the functional characteristics of genes; (2) GO annotations—evidence-supported statements asserting that a specific gene product has a particular functional characteristic; and (3) GO Causal Activity Models (GO-CAMs)—mechanistic models of molecular “pathways” (GO biological processes) created by linking multiple GO annotations using defined relations.

span.label: AND ONE TAG CARRIES ONE CLAIM, WHICH IS OUR RULE TOO: `Each GO annotation includes THE EVIDENCE upon which it is based. Because each GO annotation covers ONLY A SINGLE CHARACTERISTIC of gene function, MULTIPLE GO ANNOTATIONS ARE GENERALLY REQUIRED to completely describe the function of a gene product`
span.quote: A GO annotation ( Fig. 1b ) is an association between a specific gene (or gene product) and a GO term and should be interpreted as a statement that the specified gene product possesses the specified functional characteristic represented by the GO term. Each GO annotation includes the evidence upon which it is based. Because each GO annotation covers only a single characteristic of gene function, multiple GO annotations are generally required to completely describe the function of a gene product.

span.quote: The GO user community also plays an important role in identifying incorrect annotations. Because each annotation can be traced to the published paper containing the underlying evidence or describing a method used to infer the annotation, users can quickly verify the accuracy of a given annotation. Potential errors can be reported by clicking on the “Help” link at the top of the GO homepage ( http://geneontology.org ). In addition, authors of a paper used to create GO annotations can easily retrieve and review all annotations from a given paper and suggest changes; this can be done from the PubMed abstract page

span.label: obsoleted
span.quote: The GO is subject to constant review and revision to most accurately model the current biological knowledge. Revision of the ontology includes the addition or obsoletion of terms and reorganization of the relationship structure. New GO terms are added to represent concepts previously missing from the GO in response to published findings, or when a branch of GO is revised. Terms may be obsoleted when unused or inconsistently used in annotation, when they are redundant with other terms, or during revision of specific branches of the ontology.

span.label: the three ASPECTS as senses of `function`: `MOLECULAR FUNCTION - the activities performed by a gene product at the molecular level`; `CELLULAR COMPONENT - the LOCATIONS, relative to cellular structures, where MFs are performed`; `BIOLOGICAL PROCESS - a biological program COMPRISING MOLECULAR ACTIVITIES ACTING IN CONCERT to achieve a particular outcome`. An activity, a place and a programme, all called `function`
span.quote: The basic model underlying GO is the “molecular biology paradigm” ( Ashburner et al. 2000 ; Thomas 2017 ), in which there are three types (aspects) of functional characteristics used to describe gene function: Molecular function (MF): the activities performed by a gene product at the molecular level Cellular component (CC): the locations, relative to cellular structures, where MFs are performed Biological process (BP): a “biological program” comprising molecular activities acting in concert to achieve a particular outcome; this program can be at the cellular level or at the organism level of multicellular organisms.

Therefore, all aspects of the GO knowledgebase are dynamic (ontology, annotations, GO-CAMs, links to external ontologies, etc.), and citable, versioned updates are released on a monthly basis.

span.label: THREE SENSES OF `FUNCTION` IN ONE ONTOLOGY: molecular function is an ACTIVITY, cellular component is a LOCATION, biological process is a PROGRAMME `comprising molecular activities acting in concert to achieve a particular outcome`
span.term: THREE SENSES OF `FUNCTION` IN ONE ONTOLOGY: molecular function is an ACTIVITY, cellular component is a LOCATION, biological process is a PROGRAMME `comprising molecular activities acting in concert to achieve a particular outcome`
span.quote: The basic model underlying GO is the “molecular biology paradigm” ( Ashburner et al. 2000 ; Thomas 2017 ), in which there are three types (aspects) of functional characteristics used to describe gene function: Molecular function (MF): the activities performed by a gene product at the molecular level Cellular component (CC): the locations, relative to cellular structures, where MFs are performed Biological process (BP): a “biological program” comprising molecular activities acting in concert to achieve a particular outcome; this program can be at the cellular level or at the organism level of multicellular organisms.

span.label: `an association between a specific gene (or gene product) and a GO term ... interpreted as A STATEMENT that the specified gene product possesses the specified functional characteristic`, with `THE EVIDENCE upon which it is based`
span.quote: A GO annotation ( Fig. 1b ) is an association between a specific gene (or gene product) and a GO term and should be interpreted as a statement that the specified gene product possesses the specified functional characteristic represented by the GO term. Each GO annotation includes the evidence upon which it is based. Because each GO annotation covers only a single characteristic of gene function, multiple GO annotations are generally required to completely describe the function of a gene product.

span.label: `Terms may be obsoleted WHEN UNUSED OR INCONSISTENTLY USED IN ANNOTATION, when they are REDUNDANT with other terms, or DURING REVISION OF SPECIFIC BRANCHES of the ontology`
span.quote: The GO is subject to constant review and revision to most accurately model the current biological knowledge. Revision of the ontology includes the addition or obsoletion of terms and reorganization of the relationship structure. New GO terms are added to represent concepts previously missing from the GO in response to published findings, or when a branch of GO is revised. Terms may be obsoleted when unused or inconsistently used in annotation, when they are redundant with other terms, or during revision of specific branches of the ontology.

span.label: 3 — the ontology, the evidence-supported annotations, and the causal activity models
span.quote: The GO knowledgebase consists of three components: (1) the GO—a computational knowledge structure describing the functional characteristics of genes; (2) GO annotations—evidence-supported statements asserting that a specific gene product has a particular functional characteristic; and (3) GO Causal Activity Models (GO-CAMs)—mechanistic models of molecular “pathways” (GO biological processes) created by linking multiple GO annotations using defined relations.
